caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 736 of 2009
lawyer:
Azizul Hoq, Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner. 
None represented ------ For the Respondent
parties:
Kazim Uddin (Md)  ------ Petitioner 
Vs. 
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs and others ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J: This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the decision dated 28-1-2009 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka in Appeal N0.110 of 2004 allowing the appeal and reversing the decision dated 18-1-2004 passed by the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka in Administrative Tribunal (AT) Case No.199 of 2003 (new)/191 of 2001(old). 

 2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in a nutshell, are that on 23-6-1981, the petitioner herein joined the Police Department as a Constable. But respondent No.4 placed the petitioner under suspension with effect from 09-11-1999 on the ground of misappropriation of money which was proved by an inquiry held by Mohammad Ali, Assistant Police Commissioner. The petitioner submitted an application denying the material allegations brought against him. Without considering the written reply of the petitioner, respondent No.4 framed a charge against the petitioner on 21-11-1999 on the allegation of corruption, misconduct etc. and asked the petitioner to show cause within 7 days as to why he should not be removed from service. Accordingly, the petitioner .submitted a written statement denying the allegations brought. against him in the charge sheet. After that, the authority appointed Rafiq Ullah, Traffic Inspector as the inquiry officer who held inquiry and submitted his report recommending recovery of the misappropriated money from the salary of the petitioner. But respondent No.1 differed with the findings and decision of the inquiry officer and issued a provisional order of dismissal of the petitioner from service. Ultimately, respondent No.4 issued the order dated 01-10-2000 imposing major penalty by dismissing the petitioner from service. Being aggrieved by the order of dismissal the petitioner filed departmental appeal on 10-10-2000 to respondent No.2 which was rejected on 21-12-2000. Soon after, the petitioner also filed an application on 29-12-2000 to respondent No.1 to reinstate the petitioner in service which was also rejected by respondent No.1 on 16- 4-2001. Under the circumstances the petitioner filed AT case on 13-9-2001. 

 3. Respondent No.1 contested the case by filing a written statement denying all the allegations made in the petition contending, inter alia, that the case is not maintainable in its present form and that there is no cause of action to file the case. By observing all requirements of law, the authority issued the order of dismissal. So the case is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The Administrative Tribunal by its decision dated 18-1-2004 allowed the case. 

 8. Mr. Azizul Hoq, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the petitioner filed a review before respondent No.1 herein against the appellate order according to the newly inserted Section 7 A of the Police Officers (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 1976 (Ordinance No. LXXXIV of 1976) as amended by the Public Officers (Special Provisions) Ordinance, 1982 (Ordinance No. XXII of 1982) and as such the period of limitation would start running from the date  when the review filed by the petitioner was rejected and that the Administrative Appellate Tribunal with- out looking into this legal aspect of this case came to a finding that the case filed by the petitioner before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation. 

 10. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal came to a finding that the petitioner was dismissed from service by the authority on 01-1-2002 and that he submitted a departmental appeal on 10-10-2009 which was rejected on 21-12-2000 and that the petitioner filed Administrative Tribunal Case on 13-9- 2001. The Administrative Tribunal further came to a finding that as per Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980, the application was required to be filed before the Administrative Tribunal within 6(six) months from the date of disposal of the departmental appeal and the "departmental appeal having been rejected on 21-12-2000, the petitioner was required to file the AT case within 6 months from 21-12-2000 ,that is, before 21-6-2001 and that the AT case having been filed on 13-9-2001 is barred by limitation. 

 12. In the case in hand the petitioner filed the application in the form of a revision on 29-12-2001 to respondent No.1 according to section 7 A of the Ordinance. The petitioner was supposed to file the application before the Government and not before respondent No.1, the Inspector General of Police. Therefore the revision filed by the petitioner cannot be treated as a revision within the meaning of section 7 A of the Ordinance. 

 13. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal was, of course, wrong in holding that the petitioner was 'required to file the case before the Administrative Tribunal within six months from the date of disposal of the departmental as provided for in the provisos to section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act. In the instant case, the petitioner could not go to the Administrative Tribunal until his revision was disposed of the Government. As ill luck would have it, the petitioner made the revision to respondent No.1 and not to the Government. 

 14. A controversy may arise whether a constable comes within the definition of police officer in order to avail of the benefit of section 7 A of the Ordinance. In the schedule to the Ordinance at serial No.3, Assistant Sub-Inspector, Head Constable, Nayek and Constable have also been categorized as police officers. Therefore the petitioner could have availed of the benefit of section 7 A of the Ordinance had he filed the revision to the Government. But in the instant case the petitioner has made the revision to the Inspector General of Police which cannot be termed as a revision and as such the petitioner cannot take advantage of section 7 A of the Ordinance. 

 15. In this connection the learned Advocate for the petitioner cited the case of Shaikh Mustainul Haque vs Inspector General of Police, 47 DLR (AD) 157 in which it has been held as under: 

 "In the present case not only an appeal is provided under section 7 of the Ordinance of 1976 but also a revision from the appellate order lies to the government under section 7 A of the Ordinance as amended in 1982 therefore the appellant could not go to the Tribunal unless the Government took a decision in the matter which was evidently in the exercise of its revisional power under section 7 A. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal was therefore patently wrong in holding that the limitation could not be counted from 14-9-1989 when the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs rejected the appellant's application preferred against the appellate order passed by the Spector General of Police on 21-10-1988. It seems that the Appellate Tribunal being unaware of the aforesaid Ordinances and under some misconception of the provisos above committed error in deciding the point of limitation." 

 17. The principle expounded in the case referred to above does not apply to the facts and circumstances of the present case as the petitioner's revision was a misconceived one.
